businessObjective: Enable a logged-in customer to complete an online purchase through a checkout process that lets them review the cart, enter shipping information, review order/payment details, and confirm the order — with the process being intuitive, secure, and providing clear feedback at every step.
requirementSummary: The story defines a four-stage checkout flow (Cart Review, Checkout Information Entry, Order Overview, Order Completion), gated behind login and a non-empty cart, with mandatory-field validation and error handling on the information-entry step. Five acceptance criteria (AC1-AC5) and five business rules (BR1-BR5) are documented. Several implementation details relevant to QA scope — field validation formats, security controls, tax calculation, and cancel behavior on the information step — are not specified in the source document and are logged as Open Questions rather than assumed.

functionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall display all cart items with name, description, price, and quantity on the cart page.
The system shall display the total price calculation on the cart page.
The system shall provide options to continue shopping or proceed to checkout from the cart page.
The system shall redirect the user to the checkout information page when the "Checkout" button is clicked.
The system shall display form fields for First Name, Last Name, and Zip/Postal Code on the checkout information page.
The system shall treat all checkout information fields as mandatory.
The system shall display an error message indicating which field is required when a mandatory field is left empty and "Continue" is clicked.
The system shall redirect to the checkout overview page when "Continue" is clicked with valid checkout information.
The system shall display a summary of all items in the order on the overview page.
The system shall display payment and shipping information on the overview page.
The system shall display subtotal, tax, and total amount on the overview page.
The system shall provide options to Cancel or Finish the order from the overview page.
The system shall redirect to the order confirmation page when "Finish" is clicked.
The system shall display a success message confirming the order on the confirmation page.
The system shall display a "Back Home" button on the confirmation page to return to the products page.
The system shall display validation error messages when invalid data (special characters, incomplete information) is entered on the checkout information page.
The system shall prevent the user from proceeding until all checkout information fields are valid.
The system shall restrict access to checkout to logged-in users only.
The system shall prevent proceeding to checkout when the cart is empty.
The system shall clear the cart upon order confirmation.
The system shall allow the user to cancel checkout at any step and return to the cart.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The checkout flow shall be tested/supported across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari browsers.
The checkout flow shall be mobile-responsive.
The checkout process shall be "secure" (no concrete controls specified).
The checkout process shall be "intuitive" and provide "clear feedback" at each step.
All checkout form validation messages shall be validated as part of testing.

actors.name: Customer / Logged-in User
actors.description: Primary actor; initiates and completes the checkout flow. Represented in testing by the standard_user test credential.

actors.name: SauceDemo Application (System)
actors.description: The system under test that renders cart, checkout, and confirmation pages and enforces validation.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Cart Review
acceptanceCriteria.text:
GIVEN I am a logged-in user with items in my cart
WHEN I navigate to the cart page
THEN I should see all added items with their details (name, description, price, quantity)
AND I should see the total price calculation
AND I should have options to continue shopping or proceed to checkout

acceptanceCriteria.title: Checkout Information Entry
acceptanceCriteria.text:
GIVEN I am on the cart page with items
WHEN I click the "Checkout" button
THEN I should be redirected to the checkout information page
AND I should see form fields for First Name, Last Name, and Zip/Postal Code
AND all fields should be mandatory
WHEN I leave any field empty and click Continue
THEN I should see an error message indicating which field is required

acceptanceCriteria.title: Order Overview
acceptanceCriteria.text:
GIVEN I have entered valid checkout information
WHEN I click the "Continue" button
THEN I should be redirected to the checkout overview page
AND I should see a summary of all items in my order
AND I should see payment and shipping information
AND I should see the subtotal, tax, and total amount
AND I should have options to Cancel or Finish the order

acceptanceCriteria.title: Order Completion
acceptanceCriteria.text:
GIVEN I am on the checkout overview page
WHEN I click the "Finish" button
THEN I should be redirected to the order confirmation page
AND I should see a success message confirming my order
AND I should see a "Back Home" button to return to the products page

acceptanceCriteria.title: Error Handling
acceptanceCriteria.text:
GIVEN I am on the checkout information page
WHEN I enter invalid data (e.g., special characters, incomplete information)
THEN I should see appropriate validation error messages
AND I should not be able to proceed until all fields are valid

businessRules.rule: All checkout form fields are mandatory
Users must be logged in to access checkout
Cart cannot be empty when proceeding to checkout
Order confirmation should clear the cart
Users can cancel checkout at any step and return to cart

dependencies.notes: BR2 requires login before checkout access; login flow itself is not specified in this document.
AC1 assumes items already exist in the cart; the add-to-cart flow is out of scope of this story.
Testing depends on availability of https://www.saucedemo.com and the standard_user / secret_sauce account.

dependencies.dependency: Playwright automation framework and multi-browser test infrastructure
dependencies.notes: Required per Technical Notes to execute automated checks across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

assumptions.assumption: "Logged-in user" refers to authenticating with the provided standard_user / secret_sauce credentials.
assumptions.rationale: These are the only credentials the document supplies.

assumptions.assumption: The checkout flow implemented in the SauceDemo application maps to: Cart page -> Checkout: Your Information -> Checkout: Overview -> Checkout: Complete, matching AC1-AC4.
assumptions.rationale: Standard SauceDemo behavior; not explicitly re-described step-by-step beyond the ACs.

assumptions.assumption: No real payment is processed; "payment information" shown on the overview page (AC3) is static/demo data rather than user-entered payment details.
assumptions.rationale: The document defines no payment-entry step or payment form fields anywhere in the checkout flow.

assumptions.assumption: Only one currency and no discount/coupon/promo-code logic is in scope.
assumptions.rationale: Not mentioned anywhere in the story.

risks.risk: No Cancel control is documented for the checkout information page (AC2), yet BR5 states cancellation is possible "at any step."
risks.impact: Ambiguous scope could cause a missed requirement or an untestable acceptance criterion.

risks.risk: No validation rules (allowed characters, length, format) are defined for First Name, Last Name, or Zip/Postal Code.
risks.impact: Negative/format test cases cannot be fully specified without guessing pass/fail boundaries.

risks.risk: "Secure" checkout (Story Description) has no concrete, testable security requirement attached.
risks.impact: Security testing scope is undefined; real security gaps could go unverified.

risks.risk: Tax calculation rule/rate is not documented, despite AC3 requiring the tax amount to be displayed.
risks.impact: Correctness of the displayed tax cannot be independently verified.

risks.risk: Expected behavior for browser back/forward navigation mid-checkout is not defined, even though Technical Notes call for testing it.
risks.impact: Testers/automation would have to guess the "correct" behavior, risking false failures or missed defects.

risks.risk: SauceDemo is a public demo site with intentionally seeded bugs on certain accounts (e.g., alternate usernames not referenced here).
risks.impact: If test data/accounts change, results may reflect seeded demo bugs rather than genuine defects — out of scope for this story since only standard_user is specified.

risks.risk: No performance, load, or response-time criteria are defined for the checkout flow.
risks.impact: Non-functional test coverage for performance cannot be planned against a measurable target.

edgeCases: Attempting to proceed to checkout with an empty cart (BR3).
Leaving exactly one of First Name, Last Name, or Zip/Postal Code empty (each field individually), vs. leaving all empty.
Entering special characters, numeric-only, or oversized input into name fields.
Canceling checkout from the overview page and verifying cart contents are preserved.
Canceling checkout from the information page (if such a control exists — see Open Question OQ2) and verifying cart contents are preserved.
Verifying the cart is empty after order completion, then attempting to check out again.
Multiple line items with varying quantities, verifying subtotal/tax/total arithmetic on the overview page.
Using the browser back button after reaching the confirmation page, then attempting to re-finish the order.
Mobile-viewport execution of the full checkout flow (Technical Notes).
Session handling if login expires mid-checkout (not addressed in the source document — see Open Question OQ7).

openQuestions.question: What are the exact validation rules (allowed characters, min/max length, format) for First Name, Last Name, and Zip/Postal Code?
Does the checkout information page (AC2) expose a Cancel control, given BR5 says cancellation is possible "at any step" but AC2 lists no Cancel option?
What concrete security controls define a "secure" checkout process (e.g., transport encryption, no storage of payment data, session protections)?
What tax calculation rule or rate should the overview page apply, and how should it be verified?
Is payment method selection/entry part of this flow, or is the "payment information" on the overview page pre-populated/static demo data?
What is the expected behavior of the browser back/forward buttons at each checkout step?
What happens if the user's session/login expires while mid-checkout?
What specific devices/viewports/breakpoints define "mobile responsiveness" for the checkout flow?
Does canceling checkout guarantee the cart is preserved unchanged, or could cancellation alter cart contents?

qaCoverageRecommendations: Positive-path coverage for the full checkout flow: Cart Review -> Checkout Information -> Order Overview -> Order Completion (AC1-AC4), as a smoke/regression test.
Mandatory-field validation coverage for AC2: each of First Name, Last Name, Zip/Postal Code left empty individually, in pairs, and all together.
Negative/format validation coverage for AC5: special characters, whitespace-only input, and boundary-length input — pending clarification in OQ1 before exact pass/fail rules can be finalized.
Cart-state verification: total price accuracy on the cart page (AC1) and subtotal/tax/total accuracy on the overview page (AC3), across single-item and multi-item/multi-quantity carts.
Business-rule negative tests: attempt checkout with an empty cart (BR3) and attempt to access checkout while logged out (BR2).
Cancel-flow coverage: cancel from the overview page (AC3) and, pending OQ2, cancel from the information page — verify cart contents are preserved in both cases (BR5, OQ9).
Post-completion state check: verify the cart is cleared after order confirmation (BR4) and that "Back Home" (AC4) returns to the products page correctly.
Cross-browser execution of the above on Chrome, Firefox, and Safari (NFR1).
Mobile-responsiveness pass of the full checkout flow (NFR2), scope pending OQ8.

Exploratory testing around browser back/forward navigation during checkout (Technical Notes, OQ6) and around the undefined "secure"/"intuitive" qualities (NFR3, NFR4, OQ3) — flag findings rather than asserting pass/fail against an undocumented standard.

Do not write automated assertions against tax calculation values, Zip/Postal Code format limits, or Cancel destination from the information page until OQ1, OQ2, and OQ4 are resolved with the product owner.
